### Private Pay V1 Mainnet Pilot — planning record and architecture implications — documentation only (dated 2026-11-25; NOT authorized to execute; no source, test, schema, dependency or configuration change)

The delivery plan, workstreams (WS-0–WS-7), release gates (G0–G4), decision register and status ledger are in [docs/status/private-pay-pilot.md](docs/status/private-pay-pilot.md); the protected-staging runbook (a draft; nothing in it authorized or run) is [docs/runbooks/private-sepolia-staging.md](docs/runbooks/private-sepolia-staging.md). Target: a private, invitation-only Pay V1 pilot on Base Mainnet, **25 December 2026, conditional** — operator-only first, two or three approved external testers only after a separate release approval, no public launch. This section records only what the repository inspection at HEAD `0241bb41d04f9e2c7bbb2ba9785f3232f69bfd1b` established about the architecture's distance from that target. It decides nothing and relaxes no invariant; deployment, mainnet and every live operation stay NOT AUTHORIZED, and Real Mode stays localhost-only and testnet-only until a separate, bounded G2 approval and a control-room amendment of the testnet-only wording.

- **Status reconciliation.** The CCIP-Read hardening is **formally closed at `0241bb41d04f9e2c7bbb2ba9785f3232f69bfd1b`** (audit Verdict B, 0 Critical / High / Medium / Low, 6 accepted Info — control-room-reported). The S3 operator Turnkey read deadlines are **formally closed by explicit control-room decision on 2026-11-25** (implementation `4a3fd5a600782b216f13b659484aac3e2383ac37`; current independent closure assessment Verdict B, 0 Critical / High / Medium, 1 accepted Low, 4 accepted Info; **the original S3 documentation-audit result is unavailable and is not claimed to have passed**). The "PENDING" / "NOT closed" wording in those two sections above is the dated earlier record, left unchanged. Milestone 2 is re-identified as a private-pilot admission dependency (no implementation authorized); Milestone 3, 3C and 3D are not closed wholesale; the consolidated M3D assessment is pending. Deferred and not reopened: the `Retry-After` ceiling, Neon database deadlines, the UserOperation send-response-body deadline (Verdict E) and the backup-passkey `create_authenticators` forward (Verdict E — not the initial `CREATE_SUB_ORGANIZATION_V8`, which already has a 10-second submit abort deadline; a deadline needs a separate 2g-H replay-policy decision). Reprioritizing the UserOperation caller deadline was not approved; the deferral stands until measured staging evidence or material new evidence.
- **Network identity is hard-wired to Base Sepolia (13 production files).** Chain id 84532, the Sepolia Circle USDC address and decimals (`REAL_CASH_TOKEN`), `baseSepolia`, the explorer base URL and the Pimlico `/v2/84532/` URL appear in `lib/real/constants.ts`, `lib/real/chain/{balance,client,entry-point}.ts`, `lib/real/payments/{amount,client-sign,hash,submit}.ts`, `lib/real/server/{payments,pimlico}.ts`, `lib/stores/real-payment-store.ts` and two `components/real` files; the environment names are `BASE_SEPOLIA_RPC_URL` and `NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_SEPOLIA_RPC_URL`; a hard-coded public Sepolia RPC fallback (`https://sepolia.base.org`) is a further network-identity site, in `lib/real/server/config.ts` (a 14th file) and in `lib/stores/real-payment-store.ts`, and a missing RPC variable silently selects it; the Safe deployment (`REAL_SAFE`) is a verified Base Sepolia fact, not a mainnet one. Nothing selects a network at run time, and the chain-id guard of S5 M1 is written against 84532. A mainnet build therefore needs a scoped, audited chain-identity change (Tier A) and independently verified mainnet token, EntryPoint, Safe and paymaster identity — none of which is authorized, researched or started. External facts about Base mainnet are candidates until verified from current sources.
- **The relying-party id is permanent per account.** Passkeys are bound to `NEXT_PUBLIC_REAL_RP_ID`, which must be the exact app host (S5 M3); the browser store falls back silently to `"localhost"` if it is missing from the build. Staging and any mainnet host must be different RP IDs so no passkey spans environments, and the staging host must not be assumed to become the pilot host. What Turnkey does if the RP ID later changes is unverified.
- **Ingress has no caller authentication.** The request gate checks `Origin`, `Sec-Fetch-Site`, `Referer` and content type; it never identifies a caller. Registration is anonymous and bounded only by the 3C-1 global pool (30 per hour, 100 per day), which anonymous callers can exhaust and which is not invitation control. Any hosted copy therefore needs whole-deployment protection at the platform layer before any credential is attached (runbook §C), and an external tester needs a server-enforced approved-membership mechanism covering registration and later logins (WS-5, a Tier A design that does not exist).
- **No sponsorship or exposure policy exists in code.** Pimlico sponsorship passes no sponsorship-policy id; gas and fee ceilings (L-1 R2) and paymaster identity pinning (R3) are open; per-account provider budgets, dispatch ceilings and the 3C-1 pool are development values. **No durable, shared payment pause exists** (none found in server code or schema). The Real Mode flag is deployment configuration: a new flag-off deployment makes every Real route answer 404 only for itself, while earlier deployments keep their original configuration and credentials until retired; it is neither a project-wide kill switch nor a payment-only pause, and nothing reverses a payment or cancels remote work already started (the five separate stop layers are in the runbook, §M). Numeric limits are provisional and unapproved (pilot decision P-7); an emergency pause is undesigned (P-9) and the operator's stop procedure is undecided (P-19). *(Corrected 2026-11-27: the 2026-11-25 text called the flag "all-or-nothing", which implied a project-wide switch.)*
- **Authority and exit are not yet analyzed.** The shared parent API key and the parent's authority over child organizations are recorded S5 residuals; the development parent's root quorum is threshold 1 over two roots. Whether a user holding only their passkey could move funds if this app were unavailable is **not established by this repository** and must be answered, with a rehearsal, before G2 (WS-2, P-11). Pay by address through the app exists and is the only exit path verified in code.
- **Persistence bootstrap is unproven as one operation.** `schema.sql` is one hand-applied, idempotent, fail-closed file of 2,810 lines whose `DO` blocks are individually digest-recorded and smoke-proven on scratch schemas or one disposable branch; applying the whole file to an empty database has not been shown. Comments inside it about where blocks have been applied are historical and in places stale (the Provider Budgets, Registration Admission and Login Challenge Uses headers). It also holds three unmarked constraint-swap `DO` blocks and one one-time repair `UPDATE`; only some statements have a historical pinned digest, and the nine recorded digests use two boundary conventions (the Account Handles and Recipient Identity blocks include the trailing newline after `END $$;`; the other seven — the purpose-widening block, the `display_name` `ALTER` and the five later blocks — stop at `END $$;` or the statement's `;`; the Handles slice's own evidence list above does not state a boundary for its three pieces), recomputed and tabulated in the runbook's §F with any newly calculated reference values marked as not previously audited. A fresh isolated database needs every migration (including 3C-1) and a digest-checked, rehearsed procedure (P-13). The existing development database stays untouched.
- **Hosting and browser hardening still absent.** No script CSP (S5 requires it before any non-testnet deployment), no app HSTS, a non-`__Host-` session cookie, no `maxDuration` on any route, no recorded CDN behavior for `Content-Length` forwarding or authenticated-GET caching, and no real-device WebAuthn payload measurement. All are listed in the runbook as `[P]` research or `[L]` live checks, not as findings of fact about any provider.
- **Update 2026-11-27 (HEAD `3a5708a1d9c9ab1d3f6945c31747dc31d5d9def9`).** WS-0 is closed at that commit (independent audit Verdict B; operator-committed). **Milestone 3D is formally closed for controlled localhost Base Sepolia development by explicit control-room decision dated 2026-11-25, following the independent consolidated Verdict B** (the combined WS-0 / M3D assessment returned 0 Critical / High / Medium, 2 Low, 8 Info — combined findings, not M3D-only), with these limitations: no whole-route deadline guarantee; no guarantee of remote cancellation; every deadline value unmeasured; the four accepted deferrals (the `Retry-After` ceiling, Neon deadlines, the UserOperation send-response-body deadline, the backup-passkey `create_authenticators` forward) remain; and no automatic risk acceptance for staging or mainnet. This supersedes, for Milestone 3D only, the "M3D overall stays OPEN", "still open under M3D" and "NOT closed" wording in the dated M3D sections **above** (the Pimlico, onboarding and CCIP-Read checkpoints and the S3 section), which stay unchanged as their own dated records (the four deferrals they list remain open); no completed M3D implementation is reopened. Milestone 3, 3C and 3E stay open; L-2 E stays unauthorized. The hosting and Neon public-documentation research and the first-deployment (AR-3) checklist are in the runbook (§P, §Q); they are documentation, not verification of any account, and authorize nothing. The source fact that the installed viem's bundler send passes a per-call `retryCount: 0` stands (see the Pimlico receipt-read section); deployed and provider behavior stays unverified.
- **Process.** Tiered review (A: financial, identity, authentication, concurrency, recovery, chain configuration, migrations, ingress, security controls — design → Builder → independent combined audit → operator checkpoint; B: routine non-sensitive product work and tooling — focused review; C: ordinary documentation and runbooks) applies to the pilot track. It relaxes no existing freeze rule.

These should be decided when they're actually needed to move the project forward, with a preference for the smallest, most boring option that works — and recorded here once chosen.

## How to Use This Document

Update this file to reflect real decisions as they're made (with brief rationale), and keep the boundaries section honest — if a seam stops being real, or a candidate is verified or rejected, say so here rather than leaving stale aspirational architecture on record.
